scale: A (85+), B (70–84), C (55–69), D (45–54), F (below 45), out of 100 points per course and term.
rules: Every course is graded A–F each term from attendance, study and exams.

Attendance (40 points): the share of that course's class slots Rowan actually sat in. A skipped class is counted the moment the slot passes; being on the island but elsewhere is a skip. Sanctioned absences (representing the Academy at an event, the infirmary with a nurse's note) do not count against him.

Study (40 points): time spent studying that course outside class — in the Library (best), a dorm room, a study group, office hours. Roughly three study sessions per course every two weeks keep full marks; cramming in exam week helps less than steady work.
Exams (20 points): the midterm (advisory: its letter is posted and warns of trouble, but does not by itself fail anyone) and the final. Knowledge, preparation and a little luck on the day.

Midterms: Days 47–49 (Term 1) and 152–154 (Term 2); letters posted the following morning. Finals: Days 96–98 and 194–196; final grades posted the following morning. Exams are sat ONLY on these days, at the times and places of the exam timetable (FIXED TIMES TODAY). There are no regular classes on the exam Friday; the classes from Monday to Thursday of an exam week are revision, mock papers and office hours on that course.
Failing (F) two courses in one term means academic probation. Probation a second time, or three F in one term, means expulsion: the Chancellor's office, and the next ferry home.
Grades also matter socially: teachers treat A-students and F-students differently, some clubs and jobs ask for a minimum grade, and scholarship students need a C average.
Cheating in an exam is an automatic F and a hearing. Nobody at this school is impressed by it.
